chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zurara, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the testimony of the son for his parent and of the parent for his son, and of the brother for his brother. He said, so he said: It is allowed.
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a son or parent valid for each other in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of testimony between close kin, specifically parents and children, and siblings, reflecting the Shia juristic view that blood relation does not inherently disqualify one from being a witness. It highlights the flexibility in Islamic evidentiary rules, allowing family members to testify for one another in civil matters, provided other conditions of witness validity are met. This ruling is significant in family law contexts, such as inheritance or custody disputes, where external witnesses may be scarce.
